column1: Manatees, also known as sea cows, are aquatic mammals that belong to a group of animals called Sirenia.
column2: 海牛也被称为“海里的牛”，是海牛目的一类水生哺乳动物。

column1: This group also contains dugongs.
column2: 海牛目还包括儒艮。
column3: group|n. 类群；此处指海牛目

column1: Dugongs and manatees look quite alike – they are similar in size, colour and shape, and both have flexible flippers for forelimbs.
column2: 儒艮和海牛的外形十分相像：它们的大小、颜色和体形都相近，前肢也都是灵活的鳍肢。
column3: look quite alike|长得十分相像

column1: However, the manatee has a broad, rounded tail, whereas the dugong’s is fluked, like that of a whale.
column2: 不过，海牛的尾巴宽而圆，儒艮的尾鳍则像鲸尾一样分叉。

column1: There are three species of manatees: the West Indian manatee (Trichechus manatus), the African manatee (Trichechus senegalensis) and the Amazonian manatee (Trichechus inunguis).
column2: 海牛分为三种：西印度海牛（Trichechus manatus）、非洲海牛（Trichechus senegalensis）和亚马孙海牛（Trichechus inunguis）。
column4: West Indian manatee|n. 西印度海牛

column1: Unlike most mammals, manatees have only six bones in their neck – most others, including humans and giraffes, have seven.
column2: 海牛与大多数哺乳动物不同，颈部只有六块骨头；包括人和长颈鹿在内，其他大多数哺乳动物都有七块。

column1: This short neck allows a manatee to move its head up and down, but not side to side.
column2: 海牛的脖子短，头能上下活动，却不能左右转动。

column1: To see something on its left or its right, a manatee must turn its entire body, steering with its flippers.
column2: 要看左边或右边的东西，海牛必须用鳍肢控制方向，把整个身体转过去。

column1: Manatees have pectoral flippers but no back limbs, only a tail for propulsion.
column2: 海牛胸部有鳍肢，却没有后肢，只靠尾巴推动身体前进。

column1: They do have pelvic bones, however – a leftover from their evolution from a four-legged to a fully aquatic animal.
column2: 不过，它们的确有骨盆，这是它们从四足动物演化成完全水生的动物时留存下来的。

column1: Manatees share some visual similarities to elephants.
column2: 海牛和大象在外观上有些相似。

column1: Like elephants, manatees have thick, wrinkled skin.
column2: 像大象一样，海牛的皮肤厚而多皱。

column1: They also have some hairs covering their bodies which help them sense vibrations in the water around them.
column2: 它们身上还长着一些毛，能帮助它们感知周围水中的振动。

column1: Seagrasses and other marine plants make up most of a manatee’s diet.
column2: 海牛的食物主要是海草和其他海洋植物。

column1: Manatees spend about eight hours each day grazing and uprooting plants.
column2: 海牛每天会花大约八小时啃食水草，把植物连根拔起。

column1: They eat up to 15% of their weight in food each day.
column2: 它们每天吃下的食物最多可达自身体重的15%。

column1: African manatees are omnivorous – studies have shown that molluscs and fish make up a small part of their diets.
column2: 非洲海牛是杂食性的。研究表明，软体动物和鱼类在它们的食物中占一小部分。
column7: a small part of|……中的一小部分

column1: West Indian and Amazonian manatees are both herbivores.
column2: 西印度海牛和亚马孙海牛都是植食动物。

column1: Manatees’ teeth are all molars – flat, rounded teeth for grinding food.
column2: 海牛的牙齿全是臼齿，也就是用来磨碎食物的扁平圆齿。

column1: Due to manatees’ abrasive aquatic plant diet, these teeth get worn down and they eventually fall out, so they continually grow new teeth that get pushed forward to replace the ones they lose.
column2: 海牛吃的水生植物会磨损牙齿，牙齿因此逐渐磨耗，最终脱落。于是，海牛会不断长出新牙，新牙被推向前方，替代脱落的牙齿。

column1: Instead of having incisors to grasp their food, manatees have lips which function like a pair of hands to help tear food away from the seafloor.
column2: 海牛没有用来咬住食物的门齿；它们的双唇像一双手，能帮它们把食物从海底扯下来。

column1: Manatees are fully aquatic, but as mammals, they need to come up to the surface to breathe.
column2: 海牛完全生活在水里，但身为哺乳动物，它们需要浮到水面呼吸。

column1: When awake, they typically surface every two to four minutes, but they can hold their breath for much longer.
column2: 清醒时，海牛通常每两到四分钟浮出水面一次，但它们憋气的时间可以长得多。
column7: for much longer|长得多的时间

column1: Adult manatees sleep underwater for 10–12 hours a day, but they come up for air every 15–20 minutes.
column2: 成年海牛每天在水下睡10至12个小时，不过每隔15至20分钟就会浮出水面换气。
column5: come up for air|浮上来换气

column1: Active manatees need to breathe more frequently.
column2: 海牛活动时需要更频繁地呼吸。

column1: It’s thought that manatees use their muscular diaphragm and breathing to adjust their buoyancy.
column2: 人们认为，海牛利用由肌肉构成的膈肌，并通过呼吸来调节浮力。

column1: They may use diaphragm contractions to compress and store gas in folds in their large intestine to help them float.
column2: 它们可能通过收缩膈肌，压缩气体并将其储存在大肠的褶皱里，以帮助自己漂浮。

column1: The West Indian manatee reaches about 3.5 metres long and weighs on average around 500 kilogrammes.
column2: 西印度海牛体长可达约3.5米，平均体重约为500千克。

column1: It moves between fresh water and salt water, taking advantage of coastal mangroves and coral reefs, rivers, lakes and inland lagoons.
column2: 它往来于淡水和咸水之间，利用的栖息地包括沿海的红树林和珊瑚礁，以及河流、湖泊和内陆潟湖。

column1: There are two subspecies of West Indian manatee: the Antillean manatee is found in waters from the Bahamas to Brazil, whereas the Florida manatee is found in US waters, although some individuals have been recorded in the Bahamas.
column2: 西印度海牛有两个亚种：安的列斯海牛分布在从巴哈马到巴西的水域，而佛罗里达海牛分布在美国水域，不过巴哈马也有少数个体的记录。
column4: Antillean manatee|n. 安的列斯海牛
column7: Florida manatee|n. 佛罗里达海牛

column1: In winter, the Florida manatee is typically restricted to Florida.
column2: 冬季，佛罗里达海牛通常只在佛罗里达州活动。

column1: When the ambient water temperature drops below 20°C, it takes refuge in naturally and artificially warmed water, such as at the warm-water outfalls from powerplants.
column2: 周围水温降到20摄氏度以下时，它会躲到天然或人工加热的水域里，例如发电厂的温水排放口。

column1: The African manatee is also about 3.5 metres long and found in the sea along the west coast of Africa, from Mauritania down to Angola.
column2: 非洲海牛的体长也在3.5米左右，分布在非洲西海岸从毛里塔尼亚向南直至安哥拉的海域。

column1: The species also makes use of rivers, with the mammals seen in landlocked countries such as Mali and Niger.
column2: 非洲海牛也利用河流，在马里、尼日尔这样的内陆国家也有人见过它们。

column1: The Amazonian manatee is the smallest species, though it is still a big animal.
column2: 亚马孙海牛是海牛中最小的一种，不过它的体形仍然很大。

column1: It grows to about 2.5 metres long and 350 kilogrammes.
column2: 它的体长可达约2.5米，体重可达约350千克。

column1: Amazonian manatees favour calm, shallow waters that are above 23°C.
column2: 亚马孙海牛偏好水温高于23摄氏度的平静浅水水域。

column1: This species is found in fresh water in the Amazon Basin in Brazil, as well as in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
column2: 这种海牛分布在巴西亚马孙盆地的淡水水域，也见于哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔和秘鲁。

column1: All three manatee species are endangered or at a heightened risk of extinction.
column2: 海牛的三个物种都已濒危，或面临较高的灭绝风险。
column6: risk of extinction|n. 灭绝风险

column1: The African manatee and Amazonian manatee are both listed as Vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
column2: 国际自然保护联盟（IUCN）将非洲海牛和亚马孙海牛都列为易危物种。
column6: IUCN|abbr. 国际自然保护联盟

column1: It is estimated that 140,000 Amazonian manatees were killed between 1935 and 1954 for their meat, fat and skin, with the latter used to make leather.
column2: 据估计，1935年至1954年间，人们为了获取海牛的肉、脂肪和皮，捕杀了14万头亚马孙海牛，其中海牛皮被用来制作皮革。

column1: In more recent years, African manatee decline has been tied to incidental capture in fishing nets and hunting.
column2: 近些年，非洲海牛数量的下降与渔网误捕和猎杀有关。

column1: Manatee hunting is now illegal in every country the African species is found in.
column2: 如今，所有有非洲海牛分布的国家都已禁止猎捕海牛。

column1: The two subspecies of West Indian manatee are listed as Endangered by the IUCN.
column2: 国际自然保护联盟将西印度海牛的两个亚种列为濒危。
column6: IUCN|abbr. 国际自然保护联盟

column1: Both are also expected to undergo a decline of 20% over the next 40 years.
column2: 预计未来40年里，这两个亚种的数量也都会下降20%。
column4: are also expected to|也预计会
column7: over the next|在今后的……期间

column1: A review of almost 1,800 cases of entanglement in fishing nets and of plastic consumption among marine mammals in US waters from 2009 to 2020 found that at least 700 cases involved manatees.
column2: 一项研究回顾了2009年至2020年美国水域近1800起海洋哺乳动物被渔网缠住或吞食塑料的案例，发现其中至少700起涉及海牛。
column8: marine mammals|n. 海洋哺乳动物

column1: The chief cause of death in Florida manatees is boat strikes.
column2: 船只撞击是佛罗里达海牛死亡的首要原因。

column1: However, laws in certain parts of Florida now limit boat speeds during winter, allowing slow-moving manatees more time to respond.
column2: 不过，佛罗里达州一些地区现已依法限制冬季船速，让行动缓慢的海牛有更多时间作出反应。
